description: A stately French-inspired residential entrance photographed at twilight, evoking formal grandeur. The facade is clad in cut limestone or cream stone blocks with tight mortar joints, giving the exterior a European estate character. The front entry features a pair of tall, narrow French doors with multi-pane glass divided by slim matte-black muntins, framed within an elaborately carved limestone surround with a raised keystone detail and a carved inscription band reading an owner name or address. Above the doorway, a second-floor French door with multi-pane glass opens onto a Juliet balcony enclosed by an ornamental wrought-iron railing with scrollwork, glowing warmly from interior amber light. The steeply pitched hip roof is clad in dark grey slate tiles, and a limestone chimney stack rises from the right rear. Flanking the front door at ground level, two large dark-glazed terracotta or resin urn planters hold symmetrically clipped round boxwood topiaries. Stone entry steps with a low profile lead up to the door threshold. The sky is deep dusk blue-grey, and mature deciduous trees — their autumn foliage showing muted yellow and orange at the top left — frame the composition. Two warm pools of amber light wash symmetrically down the stone facade on either side of the entry, emanating from flanking wall positions, giving the entrance a welcoming golden glow against the dim evening sky. Camera is at a standing eye-level or slightly elevated position, centered symmetrically on the facade, using a normal lens to capture the full height of the two-story facade from entry step to roofline.
